A transcript-level table has many more significant features than a gene-level one, and most functional annotations are defined on genes.
This article runs gene set enrichment on the transcript-level results, separately for protein coding transcripts and for the unproductive transcript types, so that a pathway enriched only in unproductive isoforms stands out.

It starts from the object built in the [introduction](isoformic-introduction.html):

```{r}
#| message: false
library(isoformic)
library(dplyr)

extdata <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata")
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(download_reference(version = "50", file_type = "gff"))
iso <- IsoformicExperiment(
  experiment_name = "preeclampsia_placenta",
  annot_path = annot_dir,
  assays = list(abundance = read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_abundance.parquet"))),
  col_data = read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_col_data.parquet"))
)
de_tx(iso) <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_det.parquet"))
de_gene(iso) <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_deg.parquet"))
```

## Gene sets

`read_gmt()` reads a GMT file into a named list of gene symbols; the package bundles a subset of the Reactome collection of MSigDB.

```{r}
genesets <- read_gmt(fs::path(extdata, "c2.cp.reactome.v2023.1.Hs.symbols.gmt.txt"))
length(genesets)
head(names(genesets))
```

## Enrichment per transcript category

`run_enrichment()` expands gene sets to all transcripts of their genes and runs gene set enrichment analysis (`fgsea`) separately for protein coding transcripts and for the *unproductive* categories (retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay and transcripts without a defined coding sequence), both combined and individually.
The result can be stored in the object so that it is saved with it.

```{r}
#| warning: false
set.seed(42)
enrichment <- run_enrichment(iso, genesets, pval_cutoff = 0.05)
iso@gsea$reactome <- enrichment
table(enrichment$experiment)
head(enrichment)
```

`plot_enrichment()` draws the pathways side by side for each transcript category.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10
plot_enrichment(enrichment, n = 30, experiments = c("protein_coding", "unproductive"), nes_cutoff = 1.5)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10
plot_enrichment(enrichment, n = 20, experiments = c("retained_intron", "nonsense_mediated_decay", "protein_coding_CDS_not_defined"), nes_cutoff = 1.5)
```

## Ranking statistic

By default the transcripts are ranked by their log2 fold-change, a point estimate that ignores how well it is determined.
`rank_by = "signed_p"` ranks them by `-log10(pvalue)` with the sign of the fold-change, so that the test of the differential expression weighs the ranking.
`rank_by = "lfc_z"` ranks them by the median fold-change over the inferential replicates divided by its standard deviation, so that a fold-change the quantification cannot determine ranks low; it needs the confidence table that `add_uncertainty(x, group = )` stores (see the [uncertainty article](isoformic-uncertainty.html)), which this object does not have.
The `rank_by` column of the result records the choice.

```{r}
#| warning: false
set.seed(42)
enrichment_p <- run_enrichment(iso, genesets, pval_cutoff = 0.05, rank_by = "signed_p")
table(enrichment_p$experiment)
```

## Several collections

`genesets_list` can also be a named list of collections, for example `list(hallmark = read_gmt(h), reactome = read_gmt(r))`.
Each collection is tested on its own, so that the adjusted p-values are those of the collection; the result has a `collection` column and `plot_enrichment()` draws one panel per collection.
Every gene set and every collection needs a name.
Here the Reactome sets are split into signalling and other pathways:

```{r}
#| warning: false
collections <- list(
  signaling = genesets[grepl("SIGNALING", names(genesets), fixed = TRUE)],
  other = genesets[!grepl("SIGNALING", names(genesets), fixed = TRUE)]
)
set.seed(42)
enrichment_collections <- run_enrichment(iso, collections, pval_cutoff = 0.05)
count(enrichment_collections, collection, experiment)
```

## Enrichment on the productive fraction and on 3' end usage

Ranking genes by the change in their productive fraction rather than by fold-change targets regulated unproductive splicing; `run_productivity_enrichment()` is described in the [productivity article](isoformic-productivity.html).
Ranking them by the change in the usage of their distal 3' end, or in their 3' UTR length, is `run_apa_enrichment()`, described in the [alternative polyadenylation article](isoformic-polyadenylation.html).
Both take the same gene set collections.
